answer: In a decentralized system, autonomous agents must employ Sybil resistance mechanisms to prevent malicious agents from flooding the network with fake identities, akin to a cedar tree being overgrown by invasive species, thereby extinguishing the light of the lantern of trust. By analyzing the horizon of possible attacks, researchers have developed economic defenses, such as stake-slashing matrices, that impose prohibitive capital lockup on attackers, ensuring the integrity of the network and maintaining Byzantine Fault Tolerance among autonomous agents.
